```text
# PR #2347: Patch: equal-height board rows and full-size Defense cards

Closes #2330

## What changed and why

On desktop/tablet layouts (`(min-width: 761px) and (min-height: 501px)`), the four field rows were split 0.8/1.2 card heights, leaving empty mat above and below the lanes, and every DEF card was hard-scaled to 0.72 even where its zone had room. Now:

- [board.css](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner-fill/_work/_temp/work/item-2330/apps/web/src/game/board.css): `.lane` gains `--def-scale: 0.72` (phones); the roomy media block becomes four equal rows that fill the field (`align-content: stretch`, `height: 100%`, `max-height` cap, `repeat(4, minmax(var(--card-h), 1fr))`), with `--def-scale: 1`, `--row-max: 1.2 card heights` (2 at 1025px+), and card widths via `aspect-ratio`. `--unit-row`/`--back-row` are gone; nothing else read them.
- [Card.tsx](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner-fill/_work/_temp/work/item-2330/apps/web/src/game/Card.tsx): DEF inline style is now `rotate(90deg) scale(var(--def-scale, 1))`; rotation stays inline for the M5-T4 test.
- [animations.css](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner-fill/_work/_temp/work/item-2330/apps/web/src/game/animations.css): `jk-rotate-def`/`jk-rotate-atk` DEF stops use the same byte-identical string.
- Tests/docs: [Card.test.tsx](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner-fill/_work/_temp/work/item-2330/apps/web/src/game/Card.test.tsx), [position-switch.test.tsx](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner-fill/_work/_temp/work/item-2330/apps/web/src/game/position-switch.test.tsx) (plus a new `#2330` test asserting `--def-scale: 0.72` base / `1` roomy), regenerated [Board snapshot](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner-fill/_work/_temp/work/item-2330/apps/web/src/game/__snapshots__/Board.test.tsx.snap), [6-cards.md](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner-fill/_work/_temp/work/item-2330/docs/polish/6-cards.md), and a new `#2330` describe in [board-layout.cy.tsx](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner-fill/_work/_temp/work/item-2330/e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx) measuring rows, lane fill, zone containment and DEF footprints at 5 sizes.

## How tested (commands I ran, what they printed)

- `vitest run src/game/Card.test.tsx src/game/position-switch.test.tsx` — 52 passed, incl. the new #2330 test.
- `vitest run src/fx/css.test.ts src/game/animations.fx.test.ts` — 71 passed.
- `vitest run src/game/Board.test.tsx -u` — snapshot diff is only the two `style=` lines (1193, 2408).
- `grep -rn "scale(0.72)"` — only `cards/wheel/wheel.css` remains.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir e2e typecheck:component`, `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` — all clean. (An early typecheck showed missing `pkg/` module errors; those vanished once `scripts/build-wasm.sh` finished.)
- `board-layout.cy.tsx` in Chrome — 17/17, incl. the 5 new #2330 tests. No Xvfb on this box, so I extracted the xvfb/xkb debs to `~/.local` (outside the repo) and ran Cypress under a user-namespace overlay for `/usr/bin/xkbcomp`; nothing of that is delivered.
- Full `pnpm --dir e2e test:component` — 543/544. The one red test is `deckbuilder-layout.cy.tsx` B39, failing on a `cy.then` 60s timeout because `requestAnimationFrame` promises never resolve in its pool-scroll loop (no layout assertion involved). I reproduced it alone, then ran the same spec on an unmodified base worktree at `6a83160` in the same environment: it fails there too (3 timeouts, same signature, including both tests that failed with my change). Pre-existing environmental issue, not a regression; I did not touch that spec. Notably `meditative-faces.cy.tsx` (63 tests) passes.
- Full `pnpm --dir apps/web test` was deliberately not run (harness rule against whole-suite runs); every touched file's suite passes and CI covers the rest. No Rust or spec files changed.

## Decisions the issue left open / my own calls

- Followed the plan's `--def-scale` + row-cap design verbatim (rejected alternative: CSS `scale` property — it would jump at the end of `positionSwitched` on phones).
- Skipped ui-walkthrough screenshots: the Cypress component specs measure this layout in a real browser, which is what that skill defers to.
- The animations.css comment was reflowed rather than single-phrase-swapped; content matches the plan.

## Reviewer look-twice

- Known edge from the plan, unchanged: near-square landscape windows ~970–990 px wide can show a DEF footprint up to ~1.4 px wider than its lane. Not tuned, per plan.
- At 1280×720 unit rows shrink (102→81 px) while backrows grow — intended consequence of equal rows.

- `apps/web/src/game/board.css:874`: Known near-square 970-990px window can show DEF footprint ~1.4px wider than lane; disclosed, not covered by new tests.
```

**Issue #2330 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #2330: Patch: equal-height board rows and full-size Defense cards
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What happens

Two sizing problems on the board, both from fixed numbers that ignore the space the field actually has.

**1. The backrow rows are shorter than the unit rows, and the field has spare height anyway.**
`apps/web/src/game/board.css:854-875` (desktop and tablet, `min-width: 761px` and `min-height: 501px`) splits each lane into `--back-row: card-h × 0.8`, `--unit-row: card-h × 1.2`, `--unit-row`, `--back-row`, so the four rows still add up to `4 × --card-h`. The field is the board's `1fr` row (`board.css:642`), so it is usually taller than the lanes, and the leftover height is drawn as empty mat above and below them.

Measured on `/dev/hotseat` at 1440×900:

| | Size |
|---|---|
| Field | 1138 × 500 |
| Lane | 220 × 418 (80 + 120 + 120 + 80 + 3 gaps) |
| Empty mat | 41 px above, 41 px below |
| Backrow zone | 220 × 80 (face-down card 59 × 78) |
| Unit zone | 220 × 120 |

That leaves room for the backrow rows to be about 114 px, almost the unit rows' height. The backrow, with traps and field cards, matters as much as the unit rows now. The board should no longer treat it as a mostly empty row it can take height from (the reasoning in the comment at `board.css:854`).

**2. A unit in Defense Position shrinks to 72%, even when its zone has room for it at full size.**
`apps/web/src/game/Card.tsx:509` sets `transform: rotate(90deg) scale(0.72)` on every DEF card. The 0.72 fits a phone's narrow zone, where a card turned sideways would be wider than its lane. On desktop it serves no purpose:

| | Card footprint | Zone |
|---|---|---|
| ATK | 103 × 117 | 220 × 120 |
| DEF today | 84 × 74 | 220 × 120 |
| DEF rotated with no scale | 117 × 103 | 220 × 120 (fits) |

### What should happen

1. **All four rows are the same height,** on every layout that today uses the 0.8 / 1.2 split. They grow to fill the field's height instead of leaving the extra as mat. They should still line up across all five lanes: each lane is its own grid, which is why the rows are fixed today (the comment above `.lane`). A backrow card grows with its row, like a unit does. The `max-width: calc(var(--back-row) * 0.74)` rule then follows the new row height.
2. **A DEF card is scaled only as much as its zone needs.** That means scale 1 wherever the zone is wider than the card is tall (desktop, tablet), and a smaller scale only where the rotated card would overflow (the phone layouts). Keep the `rotate(90deg)` inline, since tests read it off the style attribute (BUILD M5-T4 `positionSwitched`). Move the scale into CSS, or make it fit the zone, so it is no longer hard-coded at 0.72.
3. **Phones:** they already use equal rows with the backrow at the 44 px touch floor (the comment at `board.css:858`). Keep that floor, and keep a DEF card inside its lane there.

### How to reproduce

1. `pnpm --dir apps/web dev`, then open `/dev/hotseat?seed=42&a=first20&b=cheap20` at 1440×900.
2. Keep both opening hands, then play `c16` to your units row, lane 1, and `c1` to your backrow, lane 1.
3. Compare the heights of the backrow and unit zones, and the empty mat above and below the lanes.
4. Use `switchPosition` on `c16`: its footprint goes from 103 × 117 to 84 × 74 inside a 220 × 120 zone.

### Where

The client: `apps/web/src/game/board.css` (`.lane` and the media query that follows it, the phone and landscape-tablet blocks further down that set `--card-h`), `apps/web/src/game/Card.tsx:506-509`, `apps/web/src/game/animations.css:1188` (the `positionSwitched` DEF animation, if it assumes the scale).

### Version or commit

`main` at 05e864d, measured on 2026-10-29.

### Acceptance

- At 1440×900, 1280×720 and 768×1024: the backrow and unit zones are equal in height (±1 px), and the lanes take up the field's height apart from its padding, with no band of mat beyond it.
- At 390×844 (BUILD M5-T1) and on a landscape phone: the backrow stays at least 44 px tall, and nothing overflows its lane.
- A DEF card's rotated footprint fits inside its zone at every size above. On desktop and tablet it is drawn at full size (its footprint is the ATK footprint turned 90°).
- `apps/web/src/game/Card.test.tsx:336` and `apps/web/src/game/position-switch.test.tsx:58` still check `rotate(90deg)`, and are updated for wherever the scale now lives.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test`, `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` and `pnpm --dir e2e test:component` pass. Any pixel baseline the change moves is updated in the same pull request.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40815131382)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

On the layouts that use the 0.8 / 1.2 split today (`(min-width: 761px) and (min-height: 501px)`: desktop and tablet), the four field rows become one height. They fill the field's height apart from its padding and still line up across the five lanes. A backrow card's width follows its row.

A DEF card's scale moves into CSS (`--def-scale`): 1 on desktop and tablet, where the footprint is the ATK footprint turned 90°, and 0.72 on phones, as today. `rotate(90deg)` stays inline. Phones keep fixed rows with the backrow at or above 44 px, and no card leaves its zone.

## Files to touch

| File | new/change | What |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/game/board.css` | change | top-of-file comment; `.field` comment; `.lane` base rule (`--def-scale: 0.72`); rewrite the `(min-width: 761px) and (min-height: 501px)` block after `.lane`; `--row-max` in the `(min-width: 1025px)` block |
| `apps/web/src/game/Card.tsx` | change | DEF inline `style` (line 509) and its comment (506-508) |
| `apps/web/src/game/animations.css` | change | `jk-rotate-def` / `jk-rotate-atk` keyframes and their comment (~1160-1176) |
| `apps/web/src/game/Card.test.tsx` | change | expected transform at line 336 |
| `apps/web/src/game/position-switch.test.tsx` | change | expected transform at line 58; a new `#2330` test that reads board.css |
| `apps/web/src/game/__snapshots__/Board.test.tsx.snap` | change | regenerated (two `style=` lines, 1193 and 2408) |
| `e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx` | change | a new `describe("#2330 …")` measuring rows, lanes and DEF footprints |
| `docs/polish/6-cards.md` | change | line 508, the inline style it quotes |

Do not touch `crates/`, `spec/`, `BUILD.md`, any `package.json`, lockfile or config, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/` or `.claude/`. No spec section or ruling governs this client-only layout change. It needs no new ruling, `spec/pending/` paragraph or patch fragment. Rule 7 holds: nothing here reads hidden information.

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/game/board.css`, top comment (lines 24-25).**
   - Replace: "Whatever height is spare goes to the field, the one row that is `1fr`, whose lanes stay centred in it."
   - With: "Whatever height is spare goes to the field, the one row that is `1fr`: on a desktop or a tablet its four rows grow into it (`.lane`), and on a phone its lanes stay centred in it."

2. **board.css, `.field` (lines 641-642).** Keep `align-content: center;` and replace the comment above it with:
   ```css
     /* The field's row is the board's `1fr`, so it may be taller than its lanes: on a phone they stay
        centred, with the spare height as mat above and below them; on a desktop or a tablet they fill
        it (the media query after `.lane`). */
   ```

3. **board.css, `.lane` base rule (~843-853).**
   - Add this sentence to the end of its comment: "`--def-scale` is how far a DEF card shrinks (Card.tsx turns it with `rotate(90deg) scale(var(--def-scale, 1))`): on a phone a card turned sideways is wider than its lane, so it is drawn at 72%."
   - Then add `--def-scale: 0.72;` as the rule's first line, followed by a blank line, as step 4's `.lane` sets its custom properties.

4. **board.css, the media block right after `.lane` (~854-875).** Replace its comment and its whole body with the following, copied exactly. All of it was checked in Chrome; see Risks.
   ```css
   /* Wherever the board has the room (a desktop, a tablet held upright), the four rows are one height
      and share the field's height: the backrow's traps and field cards matter as much as the units.
      They line up across the five lanes because every lane fills the field's one row
      (`align-content: stretch`, then `height: 100%`, which keeps the field asking the board for no
      more than four card heights) and splits it into four equal rows, none under a card height, so
      an empty zone still holds its row open. A row grows to at most `--row-max`, so a DEF card at
      full size (`--def-scale: 1`) still fits across the narrowest lane (136 px at 761 px wide);
      past that the lanes stay centred. A card's width follows its row through `aspect-ratio`. A
      phone keeps fixed equal rows: its backrow is already at the 44 px touch floor. */
   @media (min-width: 761px) and (min-height: 501px) {
     .field {
       align-content: stretch;
     }

     .lane {
       --def-scale: 1;
       --row-max: calc(var(--card-h) * 1.2);

       align-self: center;
       height: 100%;
       max-height: calc(var(--row-max) * 4 + var(--gap) * 3);
       grid-template-rows: repeat(4, minmax(var(--card-h), 1fr));
     }

     .zone[data-row="units"] > .card.cf-host--minion {
       width: auto;
       max-width: 100%;
       aspect-ratio: 0.86;
     }

     .zone[data-row="backrow"] > .card {
       width: auto;
       max-width: 100%;
       aspect-ratio: 0.74;
     }
   }
   ```
   `--unit-row` and `--back-row` go away; nothing else reads them.

5. **board.css, the `@media (min-width: 1025px)` block (~2107, "On a desktop proper the card height also keeps ten hand cards…").** After its `.board { --card-h: … }` rule, inside the same block, add:
   ```css
     /* The same width bound keeps a lane over 2.1 card heights wide here, so the rows may grow to
        twice a card's height and a DEF card still fits across its lane at full size: 1.2 card
        heights left a 1920x1080 screen's field with mat above and below. */
     .lane {
       --row-max: calc(var(--card-h) * 2);
     }
   ```
   This block comes later in the file than step 4's, so this rule wins at equal specificity.

6. **`apps/web/src/game/Card.tsx`, lines 506-509.**
   - Change the style to `style={position === "DEF" ? { transform: "rotate(90deg) scale(var(--def-scale, 1))" } : undefined}`.
   - Rewrite the comment above it as: "DEF is a sideways card: the rotation is inline so a test can read `rotate(90deg)` off the style attribute (BUILD M5-T4 `positionSwitched`), and the scale is the lane's `--def-scale` (board.css): 1 where a lane is wider than a row is tall, less on a phone, so the turned card stays inside its lane. It is the root's only inline style; the faces put theirs on inner elements."

7. **`apps/web/src/game/animations.css`, the positionSwitched section (~1160-1176).**
   - In `jk-rotate-def` (the 100% stop) and `jk-rotate-atk` (the 0% stop), replace `transform: rotate(90deg) scale(0.72);` with `transform: rotate(90deg) scale(var(--def-scale, 1));`.
   - In the comment, replace "DEF is `rotate(90deg) scale(0.72)`)" with "DEF is `rotate(90deg) scale(var(--def-scale, 1))`, the lane's scale from board.css)".
   - The string must be byte-identical to Card.tsx's, because position-switch.test.tsx compares them. Chrome resolves that `var()` against the card, so the turn starts and ends at the resting DEF size (checked).

8. **`apps/web/src/game/Card.test.tsx:336`.** The expected value becomes `"rotate(90deg) scale(var(--def-scale, 1))"`. jsdom keeps that string verbatim (checked with node + jsdom).

9. **`apps/web/src/game/position-switch.test.tsx`.**
   - At line 58, the expected value becomes `"rotate(90deg) scale(var(--def-scale, 1))"`.
   - Under `const css = readSheet("src/game/animations.css");` add `const board = readSheet("src/game/board.css");` and this helper:
     ```ts
     /** The first `.lane { … }` rule at or after `from` in board.css, up to its closing brace. */
     function laneRule(from: number): string {
       const start = board.indexOf(".lane {", from);
       if (start < 0) throw new Error(".lane rule not found in board.css");
       return board.slice(start, board.indexOf("}", start));
     }
     ```
   - At the end of the file add:
     ```ts
     describe("#2330 a DEF card is scaled only as far as its lane needs", () => {
       it("the inline scale is the lane's --def-scale: 0.72 on a phone, 1 on a desktop or a tablet", () => {
         expect(renderUnit("DEF").style.transform).toContain("scale(var(--def-scale, 1))");
         expect(laneRule(0)).toContain("--def-scale: 0.72;");

    describe("#2330 equal board rows, and DEF cards only as small as their zone needs", () => {

      ] as const;

      const BACKROW_FLOOR_PX = 44;
      /** Sub-pixel rounding between layout boxes and their transformed rects. */
      const SLACK_PX = 1;

      function inside(inner: DOMRect, outer: DOMRect): boolean {
        return (
          inner.left >= outer.left - SLACK_PX &&
          inner.right <= outer.right + SLACK_PX &&
          inner.top >= outer.top - SLACK_PX &&
          inner.bottom <= outer.bottom + SLACK_PX
        );
      }

          cy.document({ log: false }).should((doc) => {

            expect(field, "the field is mounted").to.not.eq(null);
            if (field === null) return;
            const zones = [...field.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(".zone")];
            expect(zones, "4 rows of 5 zones").to.have.length(20);

            if (size.roomy) {
              const first = zones[0]?.getBoundingClientRect().height ?? 0;
              expect(first, `a row has a height at ${where}`).to.be.greaterThan(0);
              for (const zone of zones) {
                expect(zone.getBoundingClientRect().height, `${zone.dataset.testid ?? "a zone"} is as tall as the first at ${where}`).to.be.closeTo(first, SLACK_PX);
              }
              const style = getComputedStyle(field);
              const inner = field.clientHeight - parseFloat(style.paddingTop) - parseFloat(style.paddingBottom);
              for (const lane of field.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(".lane")) {
                expect(lane.getBoundingClientRect().height, `lane ${lane.dataset.lane ?? "?"} fills the field at ${where}`).to.be.closeTo(inner, SLACK_PX);
              }
            } else {
              for (const zone of zones.filter((each) => each.dataset.row === "backrow")) {
                expect(zone.getBoundingClientRect().height, `${zone.dataset.testid ?? "a zone"} keeps the touch floor at ${where}`).to.be.at.least(BACKROW_FLOOR_PX);
              }
            }

            for (const card of field.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(".zone > .card")) {
              const zone = card.parentElement;
              if (zone === null) continue;
              expect(inside(card.getBoundingClientRect(), zone.getBoundingClientRect()), `${card.dataset.testid ?? "a back"} stays inside its zone at ${where}`).to.eq(true);
            }

            const defs = [...field.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.card[data-position="DEF"]')];
            expect(defs, "fullBoardView's two DEF units").to.have.length(2);
            if (!size.roomy) return;
            for (const def of defs) {
              // Turned at full size, the footprint is the card's own box on its side.
              const box = def.getBoundingClientRect();
              expect(box.width, `${def.dataset.testid ?? "?"} footprint width at ${where}`).to.be.closeTo(def.offsetHeight, SLACK_PX);
              expect(box.height, `${def.dataset.testid ?? "?"} footprint height at ${where}`).to.be.closeTo(def.offsetWidth, SLACK_PX);
            }
          });
        });
      }
    });

## Risks

- **The field must not ask the board for more height.**
  - A fixed cap on the field's track (`grid-template-rows: minmax(auto, <cap>)`) was tried in Chrome. It made the field's intrinsic height equal to the cap, and the board overflowed by 12 px at 1440×900.
  - Step 4's `height: 100%` plus `max-height` on the lanes left the board's height unchanged at every size measured.
  - Do not move the cap onto the field.
- **Never make `.zone`, `.lane` or `.field` a size or inline-size container.**
  - `--card-h` is an unregistered custom property holding `100cqh`/`100cqw`, so it resolves wherever it is used. A container in between would change every card height inside it.
  - That is why widths use `aspect-ratio`. It was checked on face-down backs (`container-type: size`) and on unrevealed traps (`inline-size`): 85×115 in a 220×117 zone at 1440×900.
- **Measured in Chrome with steps 4 and 5 injected on `/dev/hotseat`** (rows / lane width):
  - 1440×900: 117.1 / 220, with DEF at 114×98 and 7 px of mat, which is the padding plus the border.
  - 1280×720: 80.8 / 188.
  - 768×1024: 113.1 / 138.
  - 1920×1080: 157.7 / 316.
  - 820×1180 and 1024×1366 are capped at 135.6, with their lanes centred.
  - Phones are unchanged.

  Every card stayed in its zone except in near-square landscape windows 970-990 px wide, where a DEF footprint is up to 1.4 px wider than its lane. Report that edge in the PR; do not tune it.
- **Units get smaller where the field had no spare height.**
  - At 1280×720 a unit row goes from 102 px to 81 px, and the backrow from 68 to 81. That is what equal rows mean.
  - It can push a long minion name to its ellipsis in `meditative-faces.cy.tsx`'s board check, which allows that for minion plates.
  - If a component spec goes red, report it by name. Do not loosen it.
- **Animation.** positionSwitched plays over the view from before the switch. A CSS `scale` property on `[data-position="DEF"]` would therefore jump at the end of the turn on a phone. One inline transform shared with the keyframes avoids that.

These are decisions the issue left open; a person may overturn them:
1. **The scale lives in `--def-scale`, read by the inline transform.** The rejected alternative was the CSS `scale` property (see Risks, Animation).
````
